newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma troops overrun Karen camps, refugees flee.
newsitem.headline: Burma troops overrun Karen camps, refugees flee.

text.p: About 500 Burmese troops launched an attack on Karen National Union (KNU) guerrillas inside eastern Burma on Wednesday, sending 2,000 refugees fleeing into Thailand, rebel and Thai army sources said.
Burmese troops attacked the rebel KNU's jungle camps near the Thai border with mortars and artillery and sent troops to seize villages in the area, the source told Reuters.
The rebel KNU has been fighting the Rangoon government for greater autonomy since 1948, refused to lay down arms and rejected several peace overtures from the Burmese military.

After the troops overran two KNU positions in the morning, Burmese soldiers hit villages in the area and burned down more than three hundred houses, a school and a field hospital, a Karen refugee who fled to Thailand said.
A Thai Army officer confirmed the attack and the inflow of refugees into Thailand from Burma.
"More than 2,000 refugees have escaped fresh from fighting into Thailand today," said Colonel Suvit Maenmuan, commander of the task force responsible for the Thai-Burma border.
The rebel source said Burmese troops launched the surprise attack in areas opposite Thailand's Umphang district.
Thai army sources said the Burmese government had sent thousands of fresh troops into the area since Sunday and they expected fighting would intensify slowly.

Some 70,000 Karen refugees are already sheltered along the Thai-Burma border. They have also been hit recently by attacks from a Rangoon-backed splinter group called the Democratic Karen Buddhish Army which split from the predominantly Christian KNU in 1995.
